nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and $f : \alpha \to \beta$ a map. For every $L$-formula $\varphi$ with free variables in $\alpha$ (a bounded formula with no bound variables), Mathlib's relabelling of $\varphi$ along $f$ equals the renaming of the free variables of $\varphi$ along $f$.
nodes.title: Relabelling a formula is renaming

nodes.title: Symbols of a formula

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and $f : \alpha \to \beta$ a map. For every bounded $L$-formula $\varphi$ with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables, the set of free variables of the renaming of $\varphi$ along $f$ is the image under $f$ of the set of free variables of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Free variables of a renamed formula

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $t$ an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$, and $\varphi$ a bounded $L$-formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m + 2$ bound variables. Instantiating $t$ in the universal formula $\forall \varphi$ (which has $m + 1$ bound variables) gives the universal quantification of the instantiation of $t$ in $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Instantiation commutes with the universal quantifier

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $t$ an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$, and $i < m$. Instantiating $t$ in the term consisting of the bound variable $i + 1$ (a term with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m + 1$ bound variables) gives the term consisting of the bound variable $i$ (with $m$ bound variables).
nodes.title: Instantiation shifts the remaining bound variables down

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $t$ an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$, and $m$ a natural number. Instantiating $t$ in the term consisting of the bound variable $0$ (a term with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m + 1$ bound variables) gives $t$, regarded as a term with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m$ bound variables.
nodes.title: Instantiation at the outermost bound variable

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $t$ an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$, and $s$ an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m + 1$ bound variables $0, \dots, m$. The instantiation of $t$ in $s$ is the term with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m$ bound variables obtained from $s$ by substituting $t$ for the bound variable $0$, replacing each other bound variable $i + 1$ by $i$, and leaving the free…
nodes.title: Instantiating the outermost bound variable of a term

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $t$ an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$, and $\varphi$ a bounded $L$-formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m + 1$ bound variables $0, \dots, m$. The instantiation of $t$ in $\varphi$ is the bounded formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and $m$ bound variables obtained from $\varphi$ by instantiating $t$ in every term of its atomic subformulas: in each term, $t$ is…

nodes.summary: Relabeling variables does not change the number of leaves.
nodes.title: Relabeling variables preserves the leaf count

nodes.summary: The number of leaves of a first-order term.
nodes.title: Leaf count of a first-order term

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $M$ an $L$-structure, $v : \alpha \to M$ an assignment of the free variables, and $\varphi$ a bounded $L$-formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and one bound variable. Then the formula $\forall \varphi$ holds in $M$ under $v$ if and only if, for every $a \in M$, $\varphi$ holds in $M$ under $v$ with its bound variable set to $a$.
nodes.title: Truth of a universal formula

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $M$ an $L$-structure, and $\varphi$ a bounded $L$-formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables. If two assignments $v, v' : \alpha \to M$ agree on every free variable of $\varphi$, then for every choice of values in $M$ for the $n$ bound variables, $\varphi$ holds in $M$ under $v$ and these values if and only if it holds under $v'$ and these values.
nodes.title: Truth depends only on the free variables

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, $M$ an $L$-structure, $v : \alpha \to M$ an assignment of the free variables, $t$ an $L$-term with free variables in $\alpha$, and $\varphi$ a bounded $L$-formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and one bound variable. Then the instantiation of $t$ in $\varphi$, a formula with free variables in $\alpha$, holds in $M$ under $v$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds in $M$ under $v$ with…
nodes.title: Truth of an instance

For every assignment $v : \beta \to M$ of the free variables and every assignment $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to M$ of the bound variables, the renaming of $\varphi$ along $f$ holds in $M$ at $v$ and $x$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds in…
nodes.title: Truth of a renamed formula

nodes.summary: Let $f : \alpha \to \beta$ and let $\varphi$ be a bounded formula of a first-order language with free variables in $\alpha$ and $k$ bound variables. Mathlib's relabeling of $\varphi$ along the map $\alpha \to \beta \sqcup \mathrm{Fin}\,0$ sending $a$ to the free variable $f(a)$ replaces each free variable $a$ by $f(a)$ and produces a formula with $0 + k$ bound variables. This formula equals the renaming of…
nodes.title: Relabeling along $f$ agrees with renaming

nodes.summary: If a map $f : \alpha \to \alpha$ fixes every free variable of a bounded formula $\varphi$, then renaming the free variables of $\varphi$ along $f$ leaves $\varphi$ unchanged.
nodes.title: Renaming that fixes the free variables

nodes.summary: Given a map $f : \alpha \to \beta$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a term of a first-order language over the variables $\alpha \sqcup \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ (free variables from $\alpha$, bound variables from $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$) becomes a term over $\beta \sqcup \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ by replacing each free variable $a$ with $f(a)$ and leaving the bound variables unchanged.
nodes.title: Renaming free variables of a term

nodes.summary: Given a map $f : \alpha \to \beta$, a bounded formula $\varphi$ of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ bound variables becomes a bounded formula of $L$ with free variables in $\beta$ and the same $n$ bound variables, by replacing each free variable $a$ with $f(a)$ in every term of $\varphi$ and leaving the bound variables, the relation symbols and the logical connectives and…
nodes.title: Renaming free variables of a formula

nodes.summary: The set of symbols of a first-order language $L$ that occur in a term $t$ (with free variables and possibly bound variables), defined by recursion on $t$: a variable contributes no symbols, and $f(t_1, \dots, t_k)$ contributes the function symbol $f$ together with the symbols of the terms $t_i$. The result lies in the set of all symbols of $L$, but only function symbols can occur in a term.

Logic

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
